items.q: Also Joe Bushkin was working there. That's when he first came on the scene. He was a sixteen-year-old kid or something like that. We used to kind of look out for him, you know.

ctx.x: Yeah! Also Joe Bushkin was working there. That's when he first came on the scene. He was a sixteen-year-old kid or something like that. We used to kind of look out for him, you know. But they really snafued us. Then when everybody would go home, then they'd bring us back out. Which maybe some guys would like that, but we wanted to play. We had a good little group, you know. But that's the story of my life. Heh-heh.
So how long did that last for?

items.title: Joe Bushkin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: But at the Embers we did have Roy Eldridge and the group

ctx.x: You mean for the audience, if their bill was 20 bucks, there was a 20 percent tax on that as the war tax? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -8-

Right. But there was no tax for instrumental groups. So if a guy showed up with a party of six or eight and racked up a tab for a C note or whatever, that twenty dollars took care of the waiter’s tip and the cab ride. And so we did a lot of business, based on the fact that during the 26 week scene, we had Red Norvo’s trio and my group. I was there for the whole 26 weeks and whatever you want to call it, I was considered the draw in the place. And then we had Teddy Wilson and a group, and actually that was a…
